chapter: New York, Dallas and Kansas City
title: Two lean years in New York and playing taxi dances
summary: Moore spent about two years in New York with little work, sat in at taxi dances, and was then offered a job by Ernie Fields.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: How long were you in New York that first time?

The first time I would say I was here about two years -- two years -- until I couldn't find anything much to do because there were so many musicians -- musicians galore. So Ernie Fields came by and he asked me, he said, "How would you like to go out west again?" So, I said well --
You decided to take up on it. What did you do, though, while you were -- I guess there were long periods of time where you didn't have very much work, did you do any other kind of work?
Well, I did a few odds and ends in

different places until I joined Ernie. That was the end of that segment, the two years I spent in New York. I knew most of the musicians but they were all established in famous bands and things like that. They're not looking for anybody. They're looking for people that was better known than I was. I wasn't known then, just serving my apprentice here and there. I used to go sit in many of the taxi dance on Broadway just to keep my lip up. There used to be a guy called Bingie Madison and he played at the Tango Palace on 48th Street.
A taxi dance for the benefit of those who -- for future reference, how would you describe a taxi dance?
